hook: The president who fought the Great Depression with the New Deal and led America in the Second World War.

pages.x: Franklin Delano Roosevelt was born in 1882 at Hyde Park, New York, the only child of a wealthy family, and a distant cousin of President Theodore Roosevelt. In 1905 he married Eleanor, Theodore's niece.
In 1921, at 39, he fell ill with polio, which left his legs paralysed. He never walked on his own again, and hid it from the public. He set up a centre for polio patients at Warm Springs, Georgia.
He was elected president in 1932, in the Great Depression, when a quarter of workers had no job. At his inauguration he said: "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself."
He talked to Americans on the radio in plain words, explaining what he was doing. Families gathered around the radio to listen to his "fireside chats".
His New Deal put millions to work building dams, bridges, roads and parks, helped farmers, set rules for banks, and created Social Security, pensions for the old.
In the Second World War he sent weapons to Britain and the Soviet Union. When Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, "a date which will live in infamy", the United States joined the war.
In 1942 he ordered some 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them American citizens, into prison camps. The country formally apologised in 1988.
He won four presidential elections, more than any other president. With Churchill and Stalin he planned the defeat of Germany and Japan, and the United Nations.
He died suddenly in April 1945, weeks before victory in Europe, while sitting for a portrait at Warm Springs. The painting was never finished.

pages.x: Roosevelt led the United States through the Great Depression and the Second World War, and his New Deal built the safety net of modern America.
pts: Led America through the Depression and the Second World War
Created the New Deal and Social Security
The only president elected four times
